newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Samsung buys Australian Warrah Station.
newsitem.headline: Samsung buys Australian Warrah Station.

text.p: South Korea's Samsung Corp, a unit of Samsung Group, has bought Warrah Station, a cattle ranch in New South Wales, Australia, a Samsung spokesman said on Wednesday.
The purchase would secure a source of sustainable meat supply to meet South Korean beef demand which shows steady growth, the spokesman said.
The 15,000 acre ranch is located 340 kilometres northwest of Sydney, he said.

The company spokesman said Samsung would invest A$13 million in the ranch. The company plans to expand the livestock count to 10,000 head of cattle after 1998, compared to the current 3,000. It also aims to cultivate feed grains like wheat and rye on the ranch to enhance yields.
Samsung is expected to import beef from the ranch from 2001, when South Korea's beef market is scheduled to be opened.
South Korea supplied 47 percent of its domestic beef demand in 1995. The self-supply rate is expected to fall to 26 percent by 2000 because of a steady increase in demand, the spokesman said.
